primitives.name: Nerve Stimulation Volume Modulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the eye, intensity of nerve-stimulation seems to increase the volume of the feeling as well as its brilliancy.
primitives.assumptions: Perceptual volume scales linearly with nerve-stimulation intensity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At extreme intensities, perceptual volume saturates or distorts.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian model uses I as input to infer V; GSE maps I to perceptual state transition functions.
layer2.telemetry: Perceptual volume magnitude measured via psychophysical scaling.

primitives.name: Sensory Opacity Contraction/Enlargement
primitives.verbatim_quote: If we raise and lower the gas alternately, the whole room and all the objects in it seem alternately to enlarge and contract.
primitives.assumptions: Perceived size inversely correlates with opacity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Complete opacity results in zero visual perception.

layer2.mapping: GSI maps O to S using probabilistic sensory degradation; GSE simulates state transitions in spatial cognition.
layer2.telemetry: Change in perceived object dimensions under varying opacity.

primitives.name: Pharmacological Sensory Diminution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Morphine, atropine, daturine, and cold blunt the sensibility of the skin, so that distances upon it seem less.
primitives.assumptions: Certain drugs reduce sensory sensitivity, decreasing perceived distance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High doses may cause complete sensory loss or hallucination.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian inference links D to reduced S_d; GSE models altered body schema and spatial perception.
layer2.telemetry: Subjective distance estimation under pharmacological influence.
